name: Tulsi Gabbard
moments: He says the administration governs by press release (DHS tweets, Tulsi Gabbard, the Epstein binders, RFK Jr.'s food pyramid) and that the midterm clock was always going to run out. He argues Trump could have broken all the rules, as Stalin-style leaders do, and blew it by deferring to courts.

He says Tulsi Gabbard dodged a Senate question on whether Iran posed an imminent threat by deferring to Trump, calls it cowardice or betrayal, and says he warned that Gabbard, Rubio and the administration's picks were not America First.
I told you so. I told you that Tulsi Gabbard was not our girl.

He reads the New York Times report that Trump waved off Israel's May strike plan, including internal views of Gabbard, Wiles, Hegseth, Vance and Waltz, and Vance's view that Trump could back Israel if talks fail.

He says Hegseth's troubled nomination is dragging down other Trump picks like Gabbard, Patel and RFK Jr. in betting markets, says the cabinet is mostly bad, and says he is personally profiting from crypto under Trump.

He says Tulsi Gabbard and RFK will likely also fail, recounts the recess-appointment cope, and argues that if Republicans could not back Gaetz they will not back deportations. He portrays Trump as old, tired and apathetic, not a Caesar who will break the establishment.

He says he is ambivalent about Gaetz, suspecting he is compromised or blackmailed, and complains that Trump's appointees (RFK, Hegseth, Huckabee, Gabbard) are freaks or neocons. He says he wants clean intelligent white people running things and sounds uneasy about the administration.
